title: CRLF: the assets' eol is a contract
desiredOutcome: A Windows checkout runs the same bytes as every other platform: scripts/ui/* pinned LF in .gitattributes, and each UI module's selftest names a CRLF asset directly instead of letting a distant cross-line pin discover it.
summary: The eol of the ui/ assets is a written contract (.gitattributes eol=lf) with a guard beside each reader, red-proven via a CRLF fixture. The Windows leg's two distant pin failures trace to this one class; the readers' newline='' stays because the byte-identity proofs stand on it.

tasks.title: .gitattributes LF contract for scripts/ui + LF guard cases
tasks.description: New .gitattributes: 'plugins/audit/scripts/ui/** text eol=lf' (the assets are byte-read inputs; their eol is part of the build). Guard beside each reader: a selftest case in _panel_ui and _report_ui asserting no '\r' in any loaded asset, red-first proven via a CRLF fixture, so a future CRLF checkout is named at the reader instead of failing a distant pin. Readers keep newline='' - byte fidelity is the point.

add: assets carry LF only: CRLF fixture named red-first in _panel_ui
assets carry LF only: CRLF fixture named red-first in _report_ui

outcome.technical: Root .gitattributes pins plugins/audit/scripts/ui/** to eol=lf with the why written beside it; _cr_violations() guard in both UI modules names a CRLF asset at the reader (real-tree case green, CRLF fixture red-proof load-bearing). Readers keep newline='' - byte fidelity is the point. _panel_ui 23->25, _report_ui 17->19.
outcome.descriptive: A Windows checkout now runs the same bytes as every other platform, and if it ever does not, the selftest names the file instead of failing a pin two files away.

verifiedBy: git check-attr eol: lf on both probes
